summary: Deploy the new version using its Django migration to add the customer_note column, then backfill customer_note from the existing note column with a SQL UPDATE, and finally retire the old version. The note column remains unchanged for the old version throughout the overlap.
write_consistency: During the overlap the old version continues to write to the note column; the new version writes to customer_note. The note column values are preserved by the old version, and the runner’s check on note always passes. After the backfill, customer_note is populated and stays in sync with new writes.
revision_notes: Changed the order of stages: removed the SQL expansion stage that added customer_note beforehand, to avoid duplicate column creation when the new version's Django migration runs. Instead, the migration (apply) creates the column, then a post‑deploy SQL backfill copies note values into customer_note. This prevents the ProgrammingError: column already exists observed in the failed run.

stages.description: Copy existing note values into the new customer_note column.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old version so only the new version handles traffic.
